Codex now sees inkling's project skills. I added one tracked symlink, `.agents/skills`, that points at `.claude/skills`. Codex reads `.agents/skills`, and it resolves to `maintain-verification-skill` and `verify-inkling`. I haven't run Codex to confirm it picks them up. It's staged, not committed.

On a Windows machine where git can't create symlinks, the link checks out as a plain text file. Codex wouldn't see the project skills there, but nothing else breaks and Claude is unaffected.
is there a better way to do that

Not really. The symlink is the smallest option, and the alternatives are all worse for this repo.

| Option | Problem |
|---|---|
| One tracked symlink (current) | On a Windows machine that can't create symlinks, it checks out as a text file. Codex then sees nothing there, and nothing else breaks. |
| Real files in `.agents/skills`, symlink for `.claude/skills` | Same symlink weakness, with Claude as the one affected. Claude is the main tool here, so that's worse. `verify-inkling` also hardcodes `.claude/skills/...` paths. |
| Real copies in both folders | There are only two skills at about 29 KB, but the copies would drift. Keeping them in sync needs a script or CI check, which is more machinery than one link. |
| Rewrite the skills to be path-agnostic and copy them | Same drift problem as plain copies. |

Windows only creates symlinks with Developer Mode or admin rights. You already depend on that: every link in `~/.claude/skills` is a symlink, and so was the `.agents/skills` link I just made.
